review_notes: I read the whole target file. I also read the simp lemmas it uses in CompactFiniteTateNormSequence.lean and the downstream uses in CompactTateNormNaturality.lean. I did not run Lean. The proposed attributes are untested, in particular whether simp or reassoc would fire on the stated forms. The `_mk` lemmas state the quotient on the `QuotientAddGroup.mk` side, but their proofs use `change`, so simp may not match them syntactically. I did not report the `compactTateLimitNorm_π` direction as a defect, because `S` appears only on the right-hand side and it could not be a simp lemma.

findings.excerpt:
theorem compactTateLimitProjection_π (S : OpenNormalSubgroup G) :
    compactTateLimitProjection A L ≫
        limit.π (compactFiniteZeroDeflationDiagram A L) S =
      finiteTateZeroπ A L S := by
findings.problem: These are the canonical component equations for the limit maps. Each left side `f ≫ limit.π _ S` determines `S`, and the right side is simpler, so they are natural simp lemmas. They carry neither `@[simp]` nor `@[reassoc]`. In CompactTateNormNaturality.lean every use is hand-rolled: a `change` to an applied form, then `CategoryTheory.congr_fun` and calc chains. `limit.π_map`-style lemmas are not usable by simp here because `compactTateLimitProjection` and `compactTateLimitInclusion` are exposed defs, not `lim.map` terms.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `compactTateLimitProjection_π` and `compactTateLimitInclusion_π` with `@[reassoc (attr := simp)]`, or at least `@[reassoc]`. Their left sides are determined by `S`, so they are valid rewrite rules. `compactTateLimitNorm_π` has `S` only on its right-hand side, so it must not be simp. Add `@[reassoc]` to it and, if wanted, an elementwise variant. Callers can then replace the `change` + `congr_fun` blocks by `simp` or `rw [reassoc]`.
findings.benefit: Downstream naturality proofs (`compactTateLimitProjection_naturality`, the norm naturality lemma) could drop the `change ... at hleft/hright` boilerplate. Evidence of the workaround is at lines 178-204 of CompactTateNormNaturality.lean. The component equations become part of the default simp set for the limit maps.

findings.excerpt:
theorem relativeNorm_fullOpenNormalSubgroup
    (S : OpenNormalSubgroup G) (h : S ≤ fullOpenNormalSubgroup G) :
findings.problem: The lemma's left side contains `(fullOpenNormalSubgroup G).toOpenSubgroup`. The simp lemma `fullOpenNormalSubgroup_toOpenSubgroup` at line 43 rewrites that to `⊤`. The lemma is proved by `rfl`, so after this rewrite it says nothing. It therefore cannot serve as a simp rule: its left side is not in simp normal form. It is also unreachable by simp, so `mem_compactUniversalNormSet_iff` (lines 280-302) needs repeated `change ... at hs`/`hy` and manual `rw` with explicit `le_fullOpenNormalSubgroup` arguments. The two declarations overlap and leave the file with no simp-usable route from the full open-normal subgroup to the total norm.
findings.proposed_change: Rely on the simp lemma `fullOpenNormalSubgroup_toOpenSubgroup` (which simp can use under proof-argument congruence). Alternatively, state the relative-norm lemma with `⊤` on the left and the full subgroup recovered by simp. Then make `mem_compactUniversalNormSet_iff` use `simp [mem_universalNormSubmodule_iff]` instead of the two `change ... rw [relativeNorm_fullOpenNormalSubgroup ...]` blocks. If the lemma is kept, remove the duplicated normal-form conflict by documenting that it is for `rw` only.
findings.benefit: The simp set has one canonical form (`⊤`), and the universal-norm comparison proof no longer needs per-branch `change`/`rw` bookkeeping.

evidence.excerpt: rw [relativeNorm_fullOpenNormalSubgroup A S (le_fullOpenNormalSubgroup S)] at hy

findings.excerpt:
theorem compactTateUniversalNormQuotientEquiv_mk
    (x : group A L (⊤ : OpenSubgroup G)) :
    compactTateUniversalNormQuotientEquiv A L (QuotientAddGroup.mk x) =
      compactTateLimitProjection A L x
findings.problem: Both `_mk` lemmas are canonical computation rules, with an application on a quotient representative on the left and a simpler expression on the right. They are the only way to evaluate the descended equivalence and iso, which are exposed defs. Neither is tagged `@[simp]`. The continuity proof therefore has to call `simpa only [compactTateUniversalNormQuotientEquiv_mk]` by name. `compactTateUniversalNormQuotientIso_mk` itself needs a `change` back to the Equiv form to be proved.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp]` to `compactTateUniversalNormQuotientEquiv_mk`, and to `compactTateUniversalNormQuotientIso_mk` if its left side matches syntactically. Check this, since the proofs rely on `change` and the iso's quotient type is `CompHausAddCommGrp.quotient`. Then `compactTateUniversalNormQuotientEquiv_continuous` can use plain `simpa using hcont`. Anyone evaluating the iso on a class gets the stage-projection formula automatically.
findings.benefit: The quotient equivalence and iso reduce directly to `compactTateLimitProjection`, so later users, for example when computing with the quotient iso, need no explicit lemma citations. The remaining simp-set gap here is smaller than the first two findings, and is subject to the uncertainty about matching noted above.
